groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: Hello, doctor.
W: Hello, please take a seat. I have your test results here, and it's good news. The blood test came back clear. There is no indication of any digestive issues.
M: So then why do I feel so poorly all the time?
W: It's probably due to overwork and stress.
M: No, it can't be. I've always been working hard, but I've never felt stress. Other people suffering complain about that, but I don't. It must be something else.
W: What you have just described is a common sentiment. Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it. You told me you often work long into the night, right?
M: Yes, most days in fact. But I've been doing that for about 20 years now.
W: That doesn't matter. You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it, and now it's catching up to you.
M: But what about my feeling tired all the time and not being able to sleep well at night?
W: Those are common consequences of stress. And if you don't sleep well, then of course you will feel fatigued. I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you. They have a soft, gentle effect and are made from natural ingredients, so your stomach should tolerate them fine, and there shouldn't be any negative side effects. Take one with your dinner and come see me after a month. If there is no improvement, I'll give you something stronger.
M: Thank you, doctor.
W: That's not all. You should try and work less. Is there any way you can decrease your workload?
M: Um, I'd have to think about it. I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive. There are many things to keep track of and stay on top of.
W: I recommend you think about delegating some responsibilities to someone else. I'm not asking you to retire just to slow down a bit. It's for your own health.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: Today on People in the News, our guest is John Williams. The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player. John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25. Why did you retire so early?
M: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity. I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake. I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.
W: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career, most people wouldn't be able to resist the lure of such a high salary. When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury.
M: Not at all. It was hard to quit. I was tempted to stay in the game, because I love basketball and I loved my team. As for money, I turned professional at 18. So I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it, because I had great financial advisers. I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.
W: Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news. You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports. Why?
M: I went to university and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities. I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem. The foundation is just the latest attempt.
W: The foundation uses private donations to support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school, right?
M: Actually, we support teams for secondary school students, too, and also have some public funding.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Kate Atkinson was born in York, England, in 1951. She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author. She studied English Literature at University in Scotland. After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature. Later, she taught at the university she graduated from, and began writing short stories in 1981. She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award. The book is set in Yorkshire and has been adapted for radio, theatre, and TV. She has written two plays for a theatre in Edinburgh—the first was called Nice and the second Abandonment, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August 2000.
Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on. They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humor. Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics who become credible by virtue of being so fully realized. Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners. That is to say, comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society, where appearances count more than true moral character. A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds. The humor of a comedy of manners relies on verbal wit and playful teasing.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
Why is adaptability an important skill to exercise in the workplace? Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for. When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up. You can also serve as an example to your co-workers who may be having trouble adapting, and can help lead your team forward. Strategy consultant, Dorie Clark, explains it to us this way. "I'd say that adaptability is an important skill in the workplace because frankly, circumstances change. Competitors introduce new products, economy might enter a recession, customer preferences differ over time, and more. If you shake your fist at the sky and say why can't it stay the same, that's not going to do very much good. Instead, you need to recognise when circumstances have changed, so you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be. That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices."
Also, the workplace itself has been evolving. Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy. Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence, is a typical problem-solving technique. Employees who are unable or unwilling to participate will not easily move forward in the company. Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too. They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working. They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs, adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
What makes humans different from other species? Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development. But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine. This makes being creative a biological mandate, as what we seek in art and technology is surprise, not simply a fulfillment of expectations.
As a result, a wild imagination has characterized the history of our species. We build intricate habitats, devise complex recipes for our food, wear clothes that reflect constant changes in fashion, communicate with elaborate signs, symbols, and sounds, and travel between habitats on wings and wheels of our own design. To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key. But who innovates?
Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate. But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do. The innovative drive lives in every human brain, and the resulting war against the repetitive is what powers the massive changes that distinguish one generation from the next. The drive to create the new is a trait of being human. We build cultures by the hundreds and tell new stories by the millions. We create and surround ourselves with things that have never existed before, while animals do not. But where do our new ideas come from?
According to many, new ideas come from seemingly nowhere to great minds. From this perspective, new ideas are almost like magic. They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few. However, the reality is that, across the spectrum of human activities, prior work propels the creative process. We may think of innovation as being the result of inspiration or genius, but it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further. This happens in technology, where one invention enables or inspires further inventions. And it happens in the arts, as writers, composers, and painters use the work of previous artists in their own work. The human brain works from precedent. We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape.
What is a true creator? Is a creator a genius who makes something out of nothing? No. Creators are simply humans who use what they inherit, who absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures. Thus, humans are creators as a rule rather than as an exception.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Many dog owners would tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset, and according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right. Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time. Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations and far more serious physical conditions. This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with, and illness causes change. If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odor will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if the human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans.
Researchers have also found that a person's mood, which can be an indicator of a larger illness, triggers a dog's sense of smell. Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body, and dogs are able to smell those as well. Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person's voice in order to sense changes.
In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain similar to one in humans that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker's voice, beyond what they'd be able to pick up from familiar words alone. A person's voice can also carry indicators of illness. What's not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes. Humans send out lots of cues, but whether dogs know some of these cues mean illness isn't clear. What we perceive as concern on a dog's part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us, and sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation.
Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases, as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer. But those researchers concede that's probably in the distant future. For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself. Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood. Dogs also help people relax, and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Earlier this month, the think-tank called Onward published a report, "A Question of Degree", which argues that degrees in the creative arts are not good value for money. Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold. Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favored.
The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money. At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than 25,000 pounds a year, ten years after graduation. The average male creative arts students, indeed, apparently earn much less than they would, had they simply never gone to university. This isn't really good for anyone, and it's certainly no good for graduates, who are forced to endure a lifestyle where they can never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire.
Onward has identified a real problem. Creative arts graduates from top universities—like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately-educated students—have fairly good work prospects. Well, 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation. This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole. Regardless of what they've studied, young people find it hard to get ahead unless they're lucky enough to be born with successful parents.
If ministers want to make education pay for young people, they need to look beyond the higher education sector, towards the wider world. The rewards that education gives us are not measurable. They are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct. An education makes you a different person from the one you would have been if you hadn't received it. We need to look at the value of education not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life. If we continue to allow ourselves to be distracted with talk of "value for money", we will all be made poorer as a result.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man from his test results?
options: It is clear that he is expected to enjoy a healthy life.
There is nothing wrong with his digestive system.
There is some indication of an issue with his blood circulation.
He doesn't know he has long been suffering from poor health.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the man from his test results? 

 【翻译】 从男士的检查结果中我们了解到什么? 
 A)  很明显他有望享有健康的生活。 
 B)  他的消化系统没有任何问题。 
 C)  有迹象表明他的血液循环存在问题。 
 D)  他不知道自己长期以来一直健康状况不佳。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） There is nothing wrong with his digestive system. 
 【定位】 P2 The blood test came back clear. There is no indication of any digestive issues. 
 血液化验结果是清白的（没问题）。没有任何消化系统问题的迹象。 

 【信号】 医生宣布结果的直接陈述句 。医生一坐下就直接通报结论 The blood test came back clear 并补一句 There is no indication of any digestive issues——这种“医生直接公布检查结果”的陈述就是答案信号，不用等转折。 

 【替换】 no indication of any digestive issues ↔ nothing wrong with his digestive system “没有消化问题迹象”=“消化系统没毛病” 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 录音查的是 blood test 与 digestive issues，an issue with his blood circulation 借用了“血液 blood”的耳熟感，却把对象偷换成 blood circulation（血液循环），录音从未说循环有问题，且结果是 clear（清白），与“有问题”正好相反。  借用原文：The blood test came back clear 

 A) 过度推断 录音只说某项检查没问题，It is clear that he is expected to enjoy a healthy life 却推到“可望享有健康人生”——录音里他正feel poorly、被诊断有压力，谈不上健康一生，是无中生有的拔高。 
 D) 答非所问 He doesn't know he has long been suffering from poor health 套用了后文“压力潜伏二十年而不自知”的影子，但本题问的是 test results（化验结果），结果恰恰是“清白”，并未说明他长期体弱，错位安插。  借用原文：You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it

questions.prompt: What does the woman think is a common phenomenon among many people?
options: Mistaking symptoms of illness for stress.
Complaining they are being overworked.
Being unaware of the stress they are under.
Suffering from illness without recognising it.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman think is a common phenomenon among many people? 

 【翻译】 女士认为许多人当中有什么普遍现象? 
 A)  将疾病症状误认为是压力。 
 B)  抱怨自己工作过度。 
 C)  没有意识到自己所承受的压力。 
 D)  患病却没有察觉。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Being unaware of the stress they are under. 
 【定位】 P6 What you have just described is a common sentiment. Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it. 
 你刚才描述的是一种很常见的心态。许多承受压力的人都意识不到自己有压力。 

 【信号】 含 common / Many people 的概括句 。女方用 a common sentiment 与 Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it 对“很多人”下普遍性判断——出现 common、Many people 这类总括词，就是“普遍现象”题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it ↔ Being unaware of the stress they are under “承压却没认出”=“没意识到自己身处压力” 

 【排除】 D) 偷换概念 Suffering from illness without recognising it 与答案句框架一致（都是“X 而不自知”），但 X 被换成 illness；录音说的是 suffer from stress fail to recognise it——没认出的是压力不是疾病，差的正是那个核心变量。  借用原文：Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it 

 A) 与原文相反 Mistaking symptoms of illness for stress 是“把病当成压力”，而录音是“有压力却没认出（把压力当别的）”，方向恰好反过来；男方原话是 I've never felt stress，是不承认压力，不是错把病当压力。 
 B) 原词陷阱 Complaining they are being overworked 蹭了录音 overwork and stress 的 overwork，但女方说的是很多人“没意识到压力”，恰恰不是“抱怨过劳”；男方甚至说 other people complain，他自己不抱怨，与“很多人抱怨”相反。  借用原文：It's probably due to overwork and stress

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she will do for the man?
options: Prescribe some medication for him.
Give him another physical check-up.
Explain to him the common consequence of stress.
Buy some sleeping pills for him from the drugstore.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she will do for the man? 

 【翻译】 女士说她将为男士做什么? 
 A)  给他开一些药物。 
 B)  再给他做一次体检。 
 C)  向他解释压力的常见后果。 
 D)  从药店为他购买一些安眠药。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Prescribe some medication for him. 
 【定位】 P10 I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you. 
 我要给你开一些特制的安眠药。 

 【信号】 I'm going to + 动词的将来表态句 。女方用 I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you 主动声明下一步动作——I'm going to 这类将来式表态，就是“她将做什么”题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 prescribe some special sleeping pills ↔ Prescribe some medication for him “开安眠药”=“开药（medication）” 

 【排除】 D) 原词陷阱 Buy some sleeping pills for him from the drugstore 盗用了原句的 sleeping pills，却把动作从“医生开处方 prescribe”改成“去药店买 buy from the drugstore”；录音里医生是开方，不是替他去药店买药。  借用原文：I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you 

 C) 答非所问 Explain to him the common consequence of stress 蹭了录音 Those are common consequences of stress，但那是医生在解释失眠成因，不是回答“她将为他做什么”这一动作；本题要的是她接下来要做的事，是开药。  借用原文：Those are common consequences of stress 

 B) 未提及 Give him another physical check-up 录音从未提及再做体检——医生是看着已有的 test results 直接开药，并约一个月后复诊，没有安排再次体检。

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the industry he is engaged in?
options: It calls for responsible management.
It proves to be quite profitable.
It is remarkably promising.
It is full of competition.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about the industry he is engaged in? 

 【翻译】 男士对他所从事的行业说了什么? 
 A)  它要求负责任的管理。 
 B)  它被证明相当有利可图。 
 C)  它非常有前景。 
 D)  它充满竞争。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It is full of competition. 
 【定位】 P13 I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive. 
 我是个餐厅经理，这个行业竞争非常激烈。 

 【信号】 this industry is very + 形容词的直接评价句 。男方自陈身份后用 this industry is very competitive 直接评价所在行业——this industry is very + 形容词的结构就是“行业评价”题的答案信号，落点在 competitive 这个词。 

 【替换】 this industry is very competitive ↔ It is full of competition “非常有竞争性”=“充满竞争” 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It calls for responsible management 蹭了男方自报身份 I'm a restaurant manager 里的 manager/management，但他评价行业用的词是 competitive，从没说这行“需要负责任的管理”，是借身份词造的干扰。  借用原文：I'm a restaurant manager 

 B) 未提及 It proves to be quite profitable 谈盈利，但男方对行业的描述只有“竞争激烈”和“事务繁多”，从未提到赚钱与否，是无中生有。 
 C) 未提及 It is remarkably promising 说行业前景可观，但录音里男方谈的是竞争和繁忙、并被建议放慢节奏，全无“前景大好”之意，属凭空添加的正面评价。

questions.prompt: Why did John Williams leave the sport of basketball at just 25?
options: To avoid being in the limelight.
To seek medical help for his injury.
To pursue a less competitive career.
To stay away from his hostile teammates.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did John Williams leave the sport of basketball at just 25? 

 【翻译】 John Williams 为什么在年仅 25 岁时就离开了篮球运动? 
 A)  为了避免成为公众关注的焦点。 
 B)  为了寻求医疗帮助治疗他的伤病。 
 C)  为了追求竞争性较小的职业。 
 D)  为了远离充满敌意的队友。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） To avoid being in the limelight. 
 【定位】 P2 I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity. I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake. I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention. 
 我热爱当运动员，但我不喜欢当名人。我还在念高中时就处在聚光灯下，高中一毕业就转入职业，这是个错误。我是个害羞的孩子，还没准备好应对这一切媒体关注。 

 【信号】 被问者应答 + 转折 but 见真意 。主持人问他为何退役，被问者亲口回答的这句就是答案句；其中 but I didn't love being a celebrity 的转折 but 之后才是真正的退役理由，前半 I loved being an athlete 是铺垫干扰。 

 【替换】 I didn't love being a celebrity ↔ To avoid being in the limelight. 不爱当名人=避开聚光灯 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 借用了原文里 injury 一词，但那是主持人提出的传闻 you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury，被问者随即以 Not at all 明确否认，故因伤就医并非退役原因。  借用原文：there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury 

 C) 过度推断 他确实想趁年轻转行，但原文动机是 basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity（这行干不长），并非为追求「竞争更小」的职业，C 是无中生有地编了个理由。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D 借用原文 teammates 一词，但 issues with your teammates 同样只是主持人的猜测，被 Not at all 一并否认，与队友不和并非退役原因。  借用原文：you were having issues with your teammates

questions.prompt: What does the man say about basketball as a career for most players?
options: It has ups and downs.
It proves rewarding.
It does not last long.
It is not so profitable.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about basketball as a career for most players? 

 【翻译】 关于篮球作为大多数球员的职业,这位男士说了什么? 
 A)  它有起有落。 
 B)  它被证明是有回报的。 
 C)  它持续的时间不长。 
 D)  它没有那么赚钱。 

 【答案】 C （态度观点题） It does not last long. 
 【定位】 P4 I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young. 
 我知道对大多数球员来说，篮球不是个能干很久的职业，所以我想趁年轻就转行。 

 【信号】 被问者亲口下的定性句 。这句 basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players 是男士对篮球职业寿命的直接判断，与题干 for most players 的限定完全对应，是答案句。 

 【替换】 wasn't a career with a lot of longevity ↔ It does not last long. 缺乏长久性=持续不久 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 原文只说这行干不长，从未提到 ups and downs（有起有落），A 是凭印象编出的评价，属无中生有。 
 B) 答非所问 他确实说热爱篮球、留恋球队，但这是个人情感，并非说篮球作为职业 proves rewarding（有回报）；B 借了正面语气却与「问职业属性」答非所问。 
 D) 与原文相反 D 借用了这段反复出现的 money 话题，但原文是 I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it，说明他挺赚钱，与 not so profitable（不赚钱）正好相反。  借用原文：I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the woman about John Williams 20 years later?
options: He was a financial advisor.
He suffered from poor health.
He became a basketball coach.
He was back in the news.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the woman about John Williams 20 years later? 

 【翻译】 关于 20 年后的 John Williams,我们从这位女士那里了解到什么? 
 A)  他是一名财务顾问。 
 B)  他健康状况不佳。 
 C)  他成为了一名篮球教练。 
 D)  他重新出现在新闻中。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） He was back in the news. 
 【定位】 P5 Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news. You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports. 
 好，那是二十年前的事了，如今你重回新闻视野。你创立了一个基金会，致力于让更多孩子参与团队运动。 

 【信号】 女士口中 20 years 时间锚句 。由女士说出、带时间标志 that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news，正对应题干的 woman 与 20 years later，是答案句。 

 【替换】 you're back in the news ↔ He was back in the news. 你重回新闻=他重回新闻 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 借用了原文 I had great financial advisers 里的 financial，但那说的是他当年请了理财顾问，而非他本人 20 年后成了理财顾问，时间与身份都被错置。  借用原文：I had great financial advisers 

 B) 张冠李戴 原文谈 health 是指他后来研究 public health、关注 obesity，并非他自己 suffered from poor health；把「研究健康问题」误读成「他健康不佳」，属把内容安错对象。  借用原文：I studied public health 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 借用反复出现的 basketball，但原文 20 年后他做的是创立基金会推动孩子运动，从未说他 became a basketball coach，教练身份系无中生有。  借用原文：You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports

questions.prompt: What has the man spent the last two decades trying to do?
options: Study issues of public health.
Alleviate the obesity problem.
Raise sufficient public funding.
Train young basketball players.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has the man spent the last two decades trying to do? 

 【翻译】 这位男士在过去二十年里一直试图做什么? 
 A)  研究公共卫生问题。 
 B)  缓解肥胖问题。 
 C)  筹集足够的公共资金。 
 D)  训练年轻篮球运动员。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Alleviate the obesity problem. 
 【定位】 P6 I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities. I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem. 
 我研究了公共健康，了解到肥胖流行问题的严重性，尤其是在贫困社区的儿童和青少年中。过去二十年我一直在努力缓解这个问题。 

 【信号】 spent...trying 与题干同款行动句 。原文 I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem 与题干 spent the last two decades trying to do 几乎逐词对应，是直接锁定答案的持续行动句。 

 【替换】 trying to alleviate the problem ↔ Alleviate the obesity problem. 缓解这个问题=缓解肥胖问题 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 借用原文 I studied public health，但研究公共健康是他在大学里的学习，是认识问题的前提，而非他二十年来「致力做」的那件事；真正的长期目标是缓解肥胖。  借用原文：I studied public health 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 借用原文 also have some public funding 里的 public funding，但那只是基金会的资金来源之一，原文并未说他二十年来一直在筹集足够的公共资金，属错置内容。  借用原文：also have some public funding 

 D) 偷换概念 D 借用篮球相关词，原文确有 basketball teams 与让孩子打球，但那是缓解肥胖的手段，且对象是普通中小学生而非培养 young basketball players，目的被偷换。  借用原文：support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school

questions.prompt: When did Kate Atkinson begin to write for women's magazines?
options: When she started teaching at Edinburgh University in Scotland.
While she was doing her doctoral studies on American Literature.
After publishing her first novel Behind the Scenes at the Museum.
After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 When did Kate Atkinson begin to write for women's magazines? 

 【翻译】 Kate Atkinson 是什么时候开始为女性杂志撰稿的? 
 A)  当她开始在苏格兰爱丁堡大学任教时。 
 B)  在她攻读美国文学博士学位期间。 
 C)  在出版她的第一部小说《博物馆幕后》之后。 
 D)  在赢得1986年《女性周刊》短篇小说大赛之后。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. 
 【定位】 P1 She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. 
 她在赢得 1986 年《Woman's Own》短篇小说大赛之后,开始为女性杂志写作。 

 【信号】 after 时间标志词直接锁定时点 。答案句里 after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition 的 after 是明确的时间定向词,把"开始为女性杂志写作"这一动作精确挂在"获奖"事件之后——听到"writing for women's magazines"紧跟 after,就锁定这一句。 

 【替换】 after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition ↔ After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. 原文与选项近乎逐字同形,只需对住事件 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 When she started teaching at Edinburgh University in Scotland. 盗用了原文 she taught at the university she graduated from 这一真实事件来诱选,但任教在前(1981 写短篇之前),并非"为女性杂志写作"的时点;且原文是"母校"而非 Edinburgh University,地点也被偷改。  借用原文：Later, she taught at the university she graduated from 

 B) 原词陷阱 While she was doing her doctoral studies on American Literature. 借原文 she researched a doctorate on American Literature 设套,读博发生在 1974 年毕业后、远早于 1986 年,并非为女性杂志写作的时间。  借用原文：After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature 

 C) 原词陷阱 After publishing her first novel Behind the Scenes at the Museum. 借原文 Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award 设套;出版在 1995 年、晚于为女性杂志写作的 1986 年,时序正好反了。  借用原文：Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award

questions.prompt: What did Kate Atkinson's books touch on?
options: The themes of love and loss.
The code of human behaviour.
The sins and flaws of eccentrics.
The manners of fashionable circles.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Kate Atkinson's books touch on? 

 【翻译】 Kate Atkinson 的书涉及了什么? 
 A)  爱与失去的主题。 
 B)  人类行为的准则。 
 C)  古怪之人的罪过和缺陷。 
 D)  上流社会的礼仪。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The themes of love and loss. 
 【定位】 P2 Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on. 
 无论写什么体裁,阿特金森的书都触及爱与失、以及如何继续生活下去这些主题。 

 【信号】 题干同词 touch on 领起主题,直给答案 。答案句 her books touch on the themes of love and loss 用的动词与题干 touch on 完全同款,等于原文亲口把答案领出来——听到 "her books touch on…" 就锁这句,后面紧跟的主题即答案。 

 【替换】 the themes of love and loss ↔ The themes of love and loss. 主题表述逐字对应 

 【排除】 B) 答非所问 The code of human behaviour. 取自原文后文 the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour,但那是在解释"风尚喜剧"这一文类的定义,不是回答"her books touch on 什么主题"的内容,答非所问。  借用原文：the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society 

 C) 答非所问 The sins and flaws of eccentrics. 拼自原文 sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics,但那句讲的是书里"住着哪类人物形象",而题目问的是 touch on 的"主题",混淆了"登场人物"与"核心主题"。  借用原文：populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics 

 D) 答非所问 The manners of fashionable circles. 取自原文 code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society 与 comedies of manners,这些是解释"风尚喜剧"文类标签的措辞,而非她书的 touch on 主题。  借用原文：comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the clever and deceitful characters in a comedy of manners?
options: They are usually ignorant of complex human relations.
They successfully imitate the manners of celebrities.
They often get rewarded instead of being punished.
They are generally looked down upon in society.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the clever and deceitful characters in a comedy of manners? 

 【翻译】 关于风尚喜剧中聪明而狡诈的角色,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  他们通常对复杂的人际关系一无所知。 
 B)  他们成功地模仿名人的举止。 
 C)  他们经常得到奖赏而不是受到惩罚。 
 D)  他们在社会上普遍受到轻视。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They often get rewarded instead of being punished. 
 【定位】 P2 A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds. 
 风尚喜剧往往奖赏它那些聪明而狡诈的角色,而不是惩罚他们的恶行。 

 【信号】 reward…rather than punish 的对比定向句 。答案句用 reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds 这一"奖赏 A、而非惩罚 B"的对比结构直接交代结局——rather than 是关键定向词,把方向钉死在"受赏"一边;听到 reward…rather than punish 就锁这句。 

 【替换】 reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds ↔ They often get rewarded instead of being punished. 主动→被动 + rather than=instead of 同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They are usually ignorant of complex human relations. 把原文 the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour 里的 complex 一词揪出来拼成"对复杂人际无知",但原文从未说这些角色"无知",纯属据片词臆造。  借用原文：the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour 

 B) 未提及 They successfully imitate the manners of celebrities. 借原文 manners 一词造势,但原文只字未提这些角色"成功模仿名人",imitate/celebrities 都无出处,属凭空添加。 
 D) 与原文相反 They are generally looked down upon in society. 取了"受罚/负面"的方向,正好与原文 reward…rather than punish 的"受赏不受罚"相反——原文明说是被奖赏,本项却说被社会看轻,极性反了。  借用原文：rather than punish their bad deeds

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say adaptability is an important skill to exercise in the workplace?
options: It is what members use to alleviate tension in a team.
It is what employers are increasingly seeking after.
It is conducive to getting over a recession.
It is necessary for learning a new task.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the speaker say adaptability is an important skill to exercise in the workplace? 

 【翻译】 为什么说话者认为适应能力是在职场中需要锻炼的一项重要技能? 
 A)  这是成员用来缓解团队紧张气氛的能力。 
 B)  这是雇主日益寻求的能力。 
 C)  这有助于度过经济衰退。 
 D)  这是学习新任务所必需的。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It is what employers are increasingly seeking after. 
 【定位】 P1 Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for. 
 简单说，适应力是一种雇主越来越看重的技能。 

 【信号】 Simply put 引出总论断 。开篇自问 Why 之后紧跟 Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for，Simply put 是抛出核心结论的信号词，这句就是对 Why 的直接回答。 

 【替换】 employers are increasingly looking for ↔ employers are increasingly seeking after looking for 同义于 seeking after 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 alleviate tension in a team 在录音里根本没出现，适应力被说成雇主看重的技能而非用来化解团队紧张的工具，属凭空捏造。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音后文确念了 economy might enter a recession，但那是举例说明环境会变，并非说适应力有助于度过衰退；C 盗用 recession 制造听到就想选的诱惑，答非所问。  借用原文：economy might enter a recession 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音里 learning a new task 是说学新任务时生产力会上升，并非说适应力对学新任务必不可少；D 把这个原词搬来当重要性的理由，错位。  借用原文：When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up.

questions.prompt: What does adaptability enable us to do according to strategy consultant Dorie Clark?
options: Make better choices.
Follow innovative ideas.
Achieve recognition duly.
Accumulate work experience.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does adaptability enable us to do according to strategy consultant Dorie Clark? 

 【翻译】 根据战略顾问Dorie Clark的说法,适应能力使我们能够做什么? 
 A)  做出更好的选择。 
 B)  追随创新理念。 
 C)  及时获得认可。 
 D)  积累工作经验。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Make better choices. 
 【定位】 P1 That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices. 
 这使你能够做出更准确、更明智、更有效的选择。 

 【信号】 enables you to 的因果落点 。Dorie Clark 一番话的收尾句 That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices，enables you to 正是题干 enable us to do 的对应信号，结论就在这句。 

 【替换】 make more accurate, informed and effective choices ↔ Make better choices. 三个褒义形容词概括为 better 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Follow innovative ideas. 在 Dorie Clark 的话里没有依据，她讲的是认清变化、做出选择，未提跟随创新想法。 
 C) 未提及 Achieve recognition duly. 谈获得认可，录音从未涉及，是凭空添加的职场正能量诱饵。 
 D) 答非所问 录音说环境会变、要据实采取行动，并未提积累经验；Accumulate work experience. 借职场话题诱你联想，但答案句讲的是做选择，并非攒经验。  借用原文：you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be

questions.prompt: What do we learn about today's work culture from the passage?
options: Workers show more emotional intelligence.
Workers use brains more than muscles.
People usually work flexible hours.
People often work in teams.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about today's work culture from the passage? 

 【翻译】 从文中我们对当今的工作文化了解到什么? 
 A)  员工表现出更高的情商。 
 B)  员工更多使用脑力而非体力。 
 C)  人们通常采用弹性工作时间。 
 D)  人们经常以团队形式工作。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） People often work in teams. 
 【定位】 P2 Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy. 
 如今的工作文化和管理方式往往建立在团队合作之上，而非僵化的等级制度。 

 【信号】 Today's work culture 直接点题 。第二段开头 Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork 与题干用词几乎一致，是直接点题句，答案就在 based on teamwork。 

 【替换】 based on teamwork ↔ People often work in teams. 名词 teamwork 转为动作 work in teams 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确念了 emotional intelligence，但那是说头脑风暴需要情商，并非说工作者展现出更多情商；A 把这个原词搬来当工作文化特征，安错了对象。  借用原文：Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence 

 B) 未提及 Workers use brains more than muscles. 这种脑力对体力的对比录音从没说，是凭空臆造的常识性诱饵。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音多次出现 flexibility、flexible，但讲的是员工要灵活应变，并未说大家弹性工时；People usually work flexible hours. 借 flexible 同根词诱你联想到工时，无据。  借用原文：Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too.

questions.prompt: What are employees with adaptability able to do when changes occur?
options: Leave the group as soon as possible.
Anticipate setbacks well in advance.
Decide on new priorities speedily.
Stick to original goals confidently.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are employees with adaptability able to do when changes occur? 

 【翻译】 当变化发生时,具有适应能力的员工能够做什么? 
 A)  尽快离开团队。 
 B)  提前充分预见挫折。 
 C)  迅速决定新的优先事项。 
 D)  自信地坚持原有目标。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Decide on new priorities speedily. 
 【定位】 P2 They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working. 
 当变化发生时，他们能迅速重新排定优先级，并在某些做法行不通时提出额外的调整。 

 【信号】 when changes occur 条件句应答 。They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur 与题干 when changes occur 逐词对应，reprioritize quickly 就是对该情形的直接应答，是答案句。 

 【替换】 reprioritize quickly ↔ Decide on new priorities speedily. reprioritize=decide on new priorities，quickly=speedily 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音说有适应力的人遇变化会迅速重排优先级、自信适应，Leave the group as soon as possible. 的尽快离队是逃避态度，与原文取向相反，且 leave the group 录音未提。 
 B) 原词陷阱 录音后句确念了 regroup quickly when a setback occurs，但说的是挫折发生时迅速重整，并非 well in advance 提前预判；Anticipate setbacks well in advance. 盗用 setback 又把时间偷换成事前。  借用原文：They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs 

 D) 与原文相反 录音说 adapting to the new situation confidently，confidently 是修饰适应新情况；Stick to original goals confidently. 搬走 confidently 却接上坚持原目标，恰与适应力相反。  借用原文：adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting

questions.prompt: What question does the speaker address in this talk?
options: What differentiates people from animals.
Why philosophers disagree with scientists.
Where humans' great cognitive capacity originates.
When being creative becomes a biological mandate.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What question does the speaker address in this talk? 

 【翻译】 演讲者在本次讲话中探讨了什么问题? 
 A)  人与动物的区别是什么。 
 B)  哲学家为什么不同意科学家的观点。 
 C)  人类巨大的认知能力源于何处。 
 D)  创造力何时成为一种生物学上的必然要求。 

 【答案】 A （主旨题） What differentiates people from animals. 
 【定位】 P1 What makes humans different from other species? Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development. But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine. 
 是什么让人类区别于其他物种？一些哲学家认为是道德或伦理，而一些科学家断言是我们更高级的认知发展。但我认为，主要区别在于我们对抗常规的渴望。 

 【信号】 开篇设问 + But I argue 亮主线 。第一段以设问 What makes humans different from other species 开场，随后用 But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine 中的转折信号 But 和立场词 I argue 亮出全篇主线——这正是篇章独白"开头点题"的答案信号。 

 【替换】 What makes humans different from other species ↔ What differentiates people from animals 同义改写：different from species = differentiates from animals 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 第一段确实念到 Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development，选项 Why philosophers disagree with scientists 就盗用了 philosophers 和 scientists 这两个原词；但讲者只是借两派观点引出自己的主张，全篇根本不讨论"他们为何分歧"，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 Where humans' great cognitive capacity originates 借用了原文 our greater cognitive development 里的 cognitive；但"认知发展"是讲者复述并随即用 But 推翻的科学家旧观点，讲座既不问它"从哪来"，更没把它当主线，纯属盗词诱选。  借用原文：our greater cognitive development 

 D) 偷换概念 选项 When being creative becomes a biological mandate 搬来了原文 This makes being creative a biological mandate 的整串短语；但讲者是把"创造是生物律令"当作结论陈述，从没问它"何时"发生，选项用 When 偷换成一个录音没讨论的时机问题。  借用原文：This makes being creative a biological mandate

questions.prompt: What does the speaker believe about innovation?
options: It is what tells apart two adjacent generations.
It is what sharpens our appetite for novelty.
It is something only geniuses can achieve.
It is something every human being can do.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker believe about innovation? 

 【翻译】 演讲者对创新有何看法? 
 A)  它是区分相邻两代人的标志。 
 B)  它是激发我们对新奇事物渴望的东西。 
 C)  它是只有天才才能实现的事情。 
 D)  它是每个人都能做到的事情。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） It is something every human being can do. 
 【定位】 P3 Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate. But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do. The innovative drive lives in every human brain. 
 如今，许多人——无论外行还是专家——都认为只有天才才会创新。但我认为，创新并不是只有少数人才能做的事。创新的驱动力存在于每一个人的大脑中。 

 【信号】 But I believe + not… only a few 的立场转折 。讲者先用 many people…believe that only geniuses innovate 摆出大众看法，再以 But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do 中的 But I believe 强力转折亮出己见——转折后 + I believe 的句子正是观点题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 innovation is not something that only a few people do ↔ It is something every human being can do 否定转肯定：not only a few = every human 
 The innovative drive lives in every human brain ↔ every human being can do every human brain = every human being 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 It is what tells apart two adjacent generations 借用了原文 distinguish one generation from the next 里的 generation；但原文说的是"创新所引发的变化"区分了代际，而非"创新本身就是用来区分两代人的"，选项把因果关系改成了创新的定义，答非所问。  借用原文：distinguish one generation from the next 

 B) 原词陷阱 选项 It is what sharpens our appetite for novelty 拼用了第二段的 our appetite for novelty；但原文是"为满足对新奇的渴望，创新是关键"，是渴望催生创新，选项却反过来说"创新激起对新奇的渴望"，因果颠倒、且并非讲者对创新的核心看法。  借用原文：To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key 

 C) 与原文相反 选项 It is something only geniuses can achieve 几乎照抄原文 only geniuses innovate；但这恰是讲者用 But I believe 明确推翻的大众看法，是"与原文相反"——把讲者反对的观点当成讲者的观点，正好选反。  借用原文：many people…believe that only geniuses innovate

questions.prompt: How does the human brain work according to the speaker?
options: It seeks inspiration for novel inventions.
It constantly absorbs new information.
It uses existing ideas to create new ones.
It repeats precedent on a regular basis.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does the human brain work according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 根据演讲者的说法,人类大脑是如何运作的? 
 A)  它为新颖的发明寻找灵感。 
 B)  它不断吸收新信息。 
 C)  它利用现有想法创造新想法。 
 D)  它定期重复先例。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It uses existing ideas to create new ones. 
 【定位】 P4 The human brain works from precedent. We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape. 
 人脑依凭先例而运作。我们把继承来的想法拿来，重新组合成某种新的形态。 

 【信号】 直陈机制句 works from + take… put… into new shape 。讲者用 The human brain works from precedent 直接点出机制，又以 We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape 展开"拿旧的拼成新的"——这种正面解释"怎么运作"的句子就是细节题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape ↔ uses existing ideas to create new ones 继承的旧想法拼成新形状 = 用已有想法造新的 
 it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further ↔ uses existing ideas to create new ones 在他人想法上further发展 = 用已有想法造新 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 It seeks inspiration for novel inventions 拼用了原文 inspiration 和 one invention enables or inspires further inventions 里的词；但讲者明说新想法"几乎像魔法般灵感闪现"只是大众误解，他真正主张的是"靠先例"，故"四处寻找灵感"并非讲者的机制描述。  借用原文：They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few 

 B) 偷换概念 选项 constantly absorbs new information 听上去像"大脑怎么运作"的合理答案，且 absorb 一词原文第五段确实念到 absorb the past；但原文说的是"吸收过去/旧的东西"，选项偷换成"不断吸收新信息"，方向正好相反，差在 past 被改成 new information。  借用原文：absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures 

 D) 与原文相反 选项 repeats precedent on a regular basis 借走了原文 works from precedent 的 precedent；但讲者说的是"依凭先例去拼出新东西"，强调的是"造新"，选项却说成"只是定期重复先例"，把创造性的"用旧造新"歪曲为机械重复，与原意相反。  借用原文：The human brain works from precedent

questions.prompt: What view of many dog owners win support from researchers studying dog cognition?
options: Dogs know when their owners are not feeling well.
Dogs have the cognition for telling right from wrong.
Dogs have an aptitude for developing skills to interact with humans.
Dogs know when their human companions can no longer stand them.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What view of many dog owners win support from researchers studying dog cognition? 

 【翻译】 研究犬类认知的研究人员支持许多养狗者的哪种观点? 
 A)  狗知道它们的主人身体不适。 
 B)  狗具有辨别是非的认知能力。 
 C)  狗具有发展与人类互动技能的天赋。 
 D)  狗知道它们的人类同伴何时无法再忍受它们。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Dogs know when their owners are not feeling well. 
 【定位】 P1 Many dog owners would tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset, and according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right. 
 许多狗主人会告诉你，他们的狗不知怎么就能知道他们生病或心烦了；而据研究狗的认知的研究者所言，这些主人是对的。 

 【信号】 研究者的认定语 those pet owners are right 。答案落在研究者对狗主人看法的直接认定 those pet owners are right 上——"研究者支持哪个看法"的答案，就藏在他们说"对"所指向的那句话里，即狗能知道主人 ill or upset。 

 【替换】 their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset ↔ Dogs know when their owners are not feeling well ill or upset 概括为 not feeling well 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 telling right from wrong（分辨对错）说的是道德认知，录音通篇讲狗"感知主人健康/情绪"，从未谈狗能分辨是非，属凭常识脑补。 
 C) 原词陷阱 an aptitude for developing skills to interact with humans 借用了录音里真实出现的 an aptitude for detecting 中的 aptitude，但录音说的是"察觉变化的天赋"，不是"与人互动的技能"，是听到 aptitude 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting 

 D) 未提及 know when their human companions can no longer stand them（知道主人受不了它们了）录音从未提及，且与全文"狗体察主人健康"的暖意基调相反，属臆造。

questions.prompt: Why can dogs detect their owner's abnormal odor according to the speaker?
options: They can readily detect different ill smells of viruses.
They can easily tell what bacteria cause odor change.
They are particularly sensitive to strange smells.
They have an extremely powerful sense of smell.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why can dogs detect their owner's abnormal odor according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 根据说话者所述,狗为什么能察觉主人的异常气味? 
 A)  它们能轻易探测到病毒的各种病态气味。 
 B)  它们能容易地辨别出什么细菌导致气味变化。 
 C)  它们对陌生气味特别敏感。 
 D)  它们拥有极其强大的嗅觉。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They have an extremely powerful sense of smell. 
 【定位】 P1 If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odor will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if the human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans. 
 比如，如果一个人感染了病毒或细菌，他的气味就会变得异常，而狗能闻出这种变化，即便人闻不到，因为狗的嗅觉比人强大得多。 

 【信号】 因果信号 because 引出原因 。答案紧跟因果词 because 之后——"狗为什么闻得出"的原因就是 dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans，because 后那句即落点。 

 【替换】 dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans ↔ They have an extremely powerful sense of smell more powerful than humans 等于 extremely powerful 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 detect different ill smells of viruses 借了录音 a virus or bacteria 里的 virus，但录音只说狗能闻出气味"变了"，从没说狗能"区分不同病毒的气味"，是把原词夸大的原词陷阱。  借用原文：If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria 

 B) 原词陷阱 tell what bacteria cause odor change 用了录音的 bacteria 和 odor change，但录音说狗"闻得出气味变了"，并非"判断是哪种细菌导致的"，问的方向被偷换。  借用原文：their odor will be abnormal 

 C) 答非所问 particularly sensitive to strange smells（对怪味敏感）看似合理，但 Why 题答案严格落在 because 后的 powerful sense of smell；录音此处归因于"嗅觉强大"而非"对怪味敏感"，C 是和 D 切不开的近义干扰。  借用原文：dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with

questions.prompt: What does research suggest for now about dog ownership?
options: It can ensure owners suffer fewer chronic diseases.
It can benefit owners both physically and mentally.
It can reduce owners' risk of getting cancer or diabetes.
It can alert owners to the seriousness of their conditions.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does research suggest for now about dog ownership? 

 【翻译】 目前研究对养狗有何提示? 
 A)  它能确保主人较少患慢性疾病。 
 B)  它能在身体和心理上使主人受益。 
 C)  它能降低主人患癌症或糖尿病的风险。 
 D)  它能提醒主人注意其病情的严重性。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It can benefit owners both physically and mentally. 
 【定位】 P4 For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself. Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood. 
 就目前而言，研究表明养狗本身就能带来一系列益处。养只宠物狗已被证明能增进健康、提振心情。 

 【信号】 时间界标 For now 切出当下结论 。末段先说诊病"在遥远未来"，再用 For now 转回当下，答案落在它后面的 bolster health and boost mood——增进健康（身体）+ 提振心情（心理）。 

 【替换】 bolster health and boost mood ↔ benefit owners both physically and mentally health+mood 归纳为 physically+mentally 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 ensure owners suffer fewer chronic diseases 借了录音的 chronic diseases，但原文说狗能给"患慢病者"以慰藉 a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases，不是说养狗能"减少患慢病"，方向被偷换，且 ensure 也过强。  借用原文：they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases 

 C) 原词陷阱 reduce owners' risk of getting cancer or diabetes 借了录音 diabetes and certain types of cancer，但那是讲狗"诊断"疾病、且明说在 distant future，并非 for now 的结论；题问 for now，C 取错了时间段。  借用原文：detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer 

 D) 未提及 alert owners to the seriousness of their conditions（提醒病情有多严重）录音从未说过；末段讲的是养狗"增进健康、提振心情、给予慰藉"，没有"警示病情严重程度"一说。

questions.prompt: What does Onward's report propose ministers should do?
options: Crack down on courses like science, technology, engineering and math.
Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students.
Look at how to reform technical and vocational education.
Ensure creative arts students get better value for money.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does Onward's report propose ministers should do? 

 【翻译】 Onward的报告建议部长们应该做什么? 
 A)  严厉打击科学、技术、工程和数学等课程。 
 B)  限制创意艺术课程招收新生的能力。 
 C)  研究如何改革技术和职业教育。 
 D)  确保创意艺术专业学生获得更高的性价比。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students. 
 【定位】 P1 Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold. 
 据 Onward 称，大臣们应当"严打那些在学生毕业十年后仍只能提供极有限性价比的课程"，即在这类课程毕业生平均收入低于助学贷款偿还门槛时，限制它们招收新生的能力。 

 【信号】 建议信号 should，紧跟报告主张 。Ministers, according to Onward, should 里的 according to Onward + should 双重标记，明确这是"报告建议大臣做什么"，正是题干所问，后半 restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students 即具体动作。 

 【替换】 restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students ↔ Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students. 几乎原句保留，such courses 具体化为 creative arts courses 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项盗用了原文 crack down on courses 和 science, technology, engineering, and math 两处原词，但原文 crack down 针对的是低回报课程，而理工科恰恰是 should be favored（应受青睐）。把"打压"安到理工科头上，正负方向全反。  借用原文：Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favored. 

 C) 张冠李戴 选项盗用了第二段 looks at how to reform technical education 的原词，但那是 a government review（政府评估）的工作内容，并非 Onward 报告"提议大臣做"的事。题干问的是报告 propose 什么，主体被偷换。  借用原文：The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education 

 D) 偷换概念 选项里 24D 式的 value for money 措辞来自 ensure students get good value for money，但那同样是政府评估关注的目标，且报告主张的是"限制招生"这一具体动作，而非"确保创意艺术学生物有所值"。把整体评估目标偷换成报告的提议。  借用原文：how to ensure students get good value for money

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think of Onward's arguments?
options: Seemingly reasonable.
Clearly well-grounded.
Extremely irrational.
Apparently simplistic.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker think of Onward's arguments? 

 【翻译】 说话者如何看待Onward的论点? 
 A)  看似合理。 
 B)  明显有充分根据。 
 C)  极其不理性。 
 D)  显然过于简单化。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） Seemingly reasonable. 
 【定位】 P2 At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. 
 乍一看，Onward 的观点甚至似乎还有几分道理。 

 【信号】 让步信号 At first glance + might seem，暗示"表面有理" 。At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. 中 At first glance（乍看）与 might even seem（似乎）连用，是典型的"表面看…"让步语气，说明作者承认其"看似有理"，但保留实质判断——后文随即用数据与反驳推翻它。 

 【替换】 At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. ↔ Seemingly reasonable. seem like...have a point ↔ Seemingly reasonable，详述概括化 

 【排除】 B) Clearly well-grounded. 把作者的 seem like（似乎）拔高成 Clearly（明显）、well-grounded（根据充分）。原文有 At first glance\might even seem 的限定，恰恰说明作者认为它经不起推敲，并非"明显有理"。  借用原文：it might even seem like Onward have a point 

 C) 过度推断 Extremely irrational. 把作者温和的"看似有理但有问题"夸张成"极不理性"。原文是 might even seem like...have a point，承认其表面合理，远没到 extremely irrational 的全盘否定，态度强度严重失真。 
 D) 未提及 Apparently simplistic. 的 Apparently 蹭了原文"表面看"的味道，但 simplistic（过于简单化）这一评价原文从未给出——作者的批评是"问题不在具体学位而在整体经济"，是归因偏差，而非"简单化"。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about British college graduates five years after graduation?
options: A high proportion of them haven't tried to save money.
Most of them never hope to buy a house or to retire.
Forty percent of them earn less than ￡25,000 a year.
The majority of them have fairly well-paying jobs.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about British college graduates five years after graduation? 

 【翻译】 关于英国大学毕业生毕业五年后的情况,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  他们中很大比例没有试图存钱。 
 B)  他们中的大多数从未希望买房或退休。 
 C)  他们中40%的人年收入低于25,000英镑。 
 D)  他们中的大多数拥有薪酬相当不错的工作。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Forty percent of them earn less than ￡25,000 a year. 
 【定位】 P3 Well, 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation. 
 要知道，所有毕业生中——无论学的什么专业——有 40% 的人在毕业 5 年后年收入低于 25000 英镑。 

 【信号】 精确限定三连：40% + all graduates + 5 years after 。40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation. 同时给出百分比、人群（all graduates）、时间（5 years），三项限定与题干 five years after graduation 完全对齐，是唯一匹配句。 

 【替换】 40 percent of all graduates ↔ Forty percent of them 数字逐字对应，all graduates ↔ them 
 less than 25,000 pounds a year ↔ less than ￡25,000 a year 金额与范围词原样保留 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项盗用了 never save up 的原词，但原文是"被迫过上永远存不下钱的生活"，说的是"现状被迫如此"，并非 haven't tried to save money（没尝试去存钱）。把"存不下"偷换成"没去尝试存"，且该描述属 P2 的创意艺术生、非本题 5 年后的全体毕业生。  借用原文：never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire 

 B) 原词陷阱 选项盗用 never buy a house never hope to retire 的原词，但原文是"被迫过上永远买不起房、不敢指望退休的生活"，是被环境所迫的处境，不是 never hope to buy a house or to retire（主观上不想买房退休）。且这同样是 P2 描述创意艺术生的，与题干 5 年后全体毕业生不符。  借用原文：never buy a house, never hope to retire 

 D) 与原文相反 The majority of them have fairly well-paying jobs. 蹭了 P3 fairly good work prospects（顶尖名校创意艺术生前景不错）的原词，但那只针对牛津等顶尖名校的少数人；就全体毕业生而言原文恰恰说 40% 低于 25000，多数收入并不高。把局部的"前景好"放大成整体"多数高薪"，方向相反。  借用原文：Creative arts graduates from top universities—like Oxford...—have fairly good work prospects.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say actually accounts for the problem identified by Onward?
options: The context of a bank balance.
Britain's economy as a whole.
The specific degree a student earns.
Britain's defective educational system.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say actually accounts for the problem identified by Onward? 

 【翻译】 说话者认为什么实际上是Onward所指出问题的原因? 
 A)  银行余额的背景。 
 B)  英国整体经济。 
 C)  学生获得的具体学位。 
 D)  英国有缺陷的教育体系。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Britain's economy as a whole. 
 【定位】 P3 This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole. 
 这表明，问题其实并不在于具体学生读了什么具体专业，而真正在于整体经济。 

 【信号】 对照信号 isn't...but...，真因在 but 之后 。the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole. 用 isn't...but... 先否掉"具体专业"这个归因，再把真正原因点在 but 之后的 the economy as a whole，正对题干 actually accounts for。 

 【替换】 the economy as a whole ↔ Britain's economy as a whole. economy as a whole 几乎原词，补限定 Britain's 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 The context of a bank balance. 盗用了 P4 the value of education not in the context of a bank balance 的原词，但原文恰恰说"不要在银行账户的语境里、而要在人生的语境里看教育的价值"，bank balance 是作者要否定的衡量方式，而非问题根源。  借用原文：not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life
